summary: Data analytics and reporting in Business Central covers how to analyze and report on data: data analysis mode on lists and queries, Excel report layouts, Power BI integration and embedding, and queries as datasets or OData web services. It answers questions about choosing an analysis approach and building Excel or Power BI reports.
overview:
This section groups the options for getting insight out of Business Central data. One page compares the choices by organizational role: Power BI, data analysis on lists and queries, Excel with APIs (Power Query, PowerPivot), and report objects with Excel layouts. It is the best place to start when you need to pick an approach.

The other pages go deeper on each option. Data analysis mode lets users explore list and query data interactively without running a report. Excel layout pages explain how to create layouts and the data contract behind them. The Power BI pages describe the integration, how data is exposed through API pages and OData, and how to embed reports in pages. The query overview explains how to combine tables into one dataset and expose it as a web service.
key_points: Data analysis mode on lists and queries offers columns, filters, row groups, pivot mode, date hierarchies, and multiple analysis views, and views can be bookmarked to the Role Center.
Excel report layouts support formulas, PivotTables, PivotCharts, multiple worksheets, worksheet protection, and sensitivity labels.
The Excel layout data contract covers ExcelLayoutMultipleDataSheets, system worksheets, translations, named formulas, and drillthrough.
Power BI reports, scorecards, and dashboards can be embedded in pages using the Power BI embed framework, for example Power BI Embedded Report Part and Power BI Element Addin Host.
Embedded Power BI content can be tied to page context with SetCurrentListSelection and SetPageContext.
Business Central data reaches Power BI through API pages and OData, the Power Query connector, dataflows and datamarts, and Power BI Desktop.
Queries combine records from one or more tables, support totals and grouping, and come as normal queries or API queries that can be exposed as OData web services.
